questions.stem:
[In this question $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are horizontal unit vectors due east and due north respectively and position vectors are given relative to a fixed origin $O$.]

At time $t=0$, a bird $A$ leaves its nest, that is located at the point with position vector $(20\mathbf{i}-17\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m}$, and flies with constant velocity $(-6\mathbf{i}+7\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. At the same time a second bird $B$ leaves its nest which is located at the point with position vector $(-8\mathbf{i}+9\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m}$ and flies with constant velocity $(p\mathbf{i}+2p\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, where $p$ is a constant. At time $t=4\,\mathrm{s}$, bird $B$ is south west of bird $A$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the direction of motion of $A$, giving your answer as a bearing to the nearest degree.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme: (a) M1: any trig ratio using 6 and 7: $\tan\theta=\pm\frac{6}{7}$ or $\pm\frac{7}{6}$: $\sin\theta$ or $\cos\theta=\pm\frac{6}{\sqrt{6^2+7^2}}$ or $\pm\frac{7}{\sqrt{6^2+7^2}}$. $\tan\theta=\frac{6}{7}$, $\theta\approx 40.6^\circ$. A1: correct angle from their correct equation e.g. $49^\circ, 41^\circ, 139^\circ, 131^\circ,...$ Bearing is $360^\circ-40.6^\circ=319^\circ$ nearest degree. A1: $319^\circ$ cao.

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme: (b) $\mathbf{r}_A=(20\mathbf{i}-17\mathbf{j})+4(-6\mathbf{i}+7\mathbf{j})=(-4\mathbf{i}+11\mathbf{j})$ M1: attempt at use of $\mathbf{r}_4=\mathbf{r}_0+4\mathbf{v}$ for either $A$ or $B$. A1: $(-4\mathbf{i}+11\mathbf{j})$, $\mathbf{i}$'s and $\mathbf{j}$'s must be collected at some stage. $\mathbf{r}_B=(-8\mathbf{i}+9\mathbf{j})+4(p\mathbf{i}+2p\mathbf{j})=(-8+4p)\mathbf{i}+(9+8p)\mathbf{j}$ A1: $(-8+4p)\mathbf{i}+(9+8p)\mathbf{j}$, $\mathbf{i}$'s and $\mathbf{j}$'s must be collected at some stage. $\mathbf{r}_A-\mathbf{r}_B=(4-4p)\mathbf{i}+(2-8p)\mathbf{j}$ DM1: dependent on first M1, for finding the difference between their two $\mathbf{r}_4$ vectors (must be an attempt to subtract both $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ components). $-8+4p--4=9+8p-11$ M1: equating the $\mathbf{i}$ cpt and $\mathbf{j}$ cpt of their difference (M0 if no difference) to give an equation in $p$ only. oe, e.g. $\frac{(4-4p)}{(2-8p)}=\frac{(-)1}{(-)1}$. A1: correct equation in $p$ only. $p=-0.5$ A1: correct value of $p$. $\mathbf{v}_B=(-0.5\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j})$ M1: using their $p$ value to obtain a velocity vector for $B$. $|\mathbf{v}_B|=\sqrt{(-0.5)^2+(-1)^2}$ M1: finding the magnitude of their $\mathbf{v}_B$ (N.B. This M mark is available, even if their $\mathbf{v}_B$ does not have the correct form). $=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}\approx 1.1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ or better A1: $\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}$ oe or 1.1 or better.

questions.stem: A lift of mass $M\,\mathrm{kg}$ is being raised by a vertical cable attached to the top of the lift. A person of mass $m\,\mathrm{kg}$ stands on the floor inside the lift, as shown in Figure 1. The lift ascends vertically with constant acceleration $1.4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. The tension in the cable is $2800\,\mathrm{N}$ and the person experiences a constant normal reaction of magnitude $560\,\mathrm{N}$ from the floor of the lift. The cable is modelled as being light and inextensible, the person is modelled as a particle and air resistance is negligible.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Write down an equation of motion for the person only.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: (a) $560-mg=1.4m$ M1: equation of motion for the person only, with usual rules, condone sign errors, and with at least one value (560 or 1.4) substituted. Credit given for this equation only if it appears in (a). A1: correct equation.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Write down an equation of motion for the lift only.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: (b) $2800-Mg-560=1.4M$ M1: equation of motion for the lift only, with usual rules, condone sign errors, and with at least one value (2800, 560 or 1.4) substituted. Credit given for this equation only if it appears in (b). A1: correct equation.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Hence, or otherwise, find
(i) the value of $m$,
(ii) the value of $M$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme: (c)(i) Using $560-mg=1.4m$, i.e. $560=(g+1.4)m$ DM1 (Hence): dependent on appropriate previous M mark, for solving one of their equations, wherever it appears, for either $m$ or $M$. (Otherwise): DM1, dependent on appropriate previous M mark, for solving one of their equations and/or the whole system equation, wherever they appear, for either $m$ or $M$. N.B. There are no marks available for the whole system equation. $m=50$ A1: $m=50$. (ii) Using $2800-Mg-560=1.4M$, i.e. $2240=(g+1.4)M$, $M=200$ A1: $M=200$.

questions.stem:
A boy sees a box on the end $Q$ of a plank $PQ$ which overhangs a swimming pool. The plank has mass $30\,\mathrm{kg}$, is $5\,\mathrm{m}$ long and rests in a horizontal position on two bricks. The bricks are modelled as smooth supports, one acting on the rod at $P$ and one acting on the rod at $R$, where $PR=3\,\mathrm{m}$. The support at $R$ is on the edge of the swimming pool, as shown in Figure 2. The boy has mass $40\,\mathrm{kg}$ and the box has mass $2.5\,\mathrm{kg}$. The plank is modelled as a uniform rod and the boy and the box are modelled as particles.

The boy steps on to the plank at $P$ and begins to walk slowly along the plank towards the box.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the distance he can walk along the plank from $P$ before the plank starts to tilt.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme: (a) $M(R)$: $40g(x-3)+2.5g\times 2=30g\times 0.5$ M1: moments about $R$ to give an equation in $x$ (or another unknown distance) only (i.e. M0 if reaction at $P$ is non-zero). Correct no. of terms, dimensionally correct. A2: correct equation in $x$ only (allow consistent omission of $g$) -1 each error. Alternative: instead of $M(R)$, may write down 2 equations and eliminate the normal reaction at $R$, $N_R$, to obtain an equation in a distance only: $(\uparrow)N_R=40g+30g+2.5g$; $M(P)$: $40gx+30g\times 2.5+2.5g\times 5=3N_R$; $M(Q)$: $40g(5-x)+30g\times 2.5=2N_R$; $M(G)$: $40g(2.5-x)+0.5N_R=2.5g\times 2.5$. Equations must have correct no. of terms and be dimensionally correct but M0 if reaction at $P$ is non-zero. $x=\frac{13}{4}$ m from $P$ A1: $\frac{13}{4}$ m oe. Allow 3.3 m.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) State how you have used, in your working, the fact that the box is modelled as a particle.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: (b) B1: Mass of the box is concentrated at the point $Q$ oe. B1 for mass or weight of box acts at $Q$ but B0 if extra wrong answers.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
A rock of mass $M\,\mathrm{kg}$ is placed on the plank at $P$. The boy is then able to walk slowly along the plank to the box at the end $Q$ without the plank tilting. The rock is modelled as a particle.

(c) Find the smallest possible value of $M$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme: (c) $M(R)$: $3Mg+30g\times 0.5=2.5g\times 2+40g\times 2$ M1: moments about $R$ to give an equation in $M$ only (i.e. M0 if reaction at $P$ is non-zero). Correct no. of terms, dimensionally correct. A2: correct equation in $M$ only (allow consistent omission of $g$) -1 each error. Alternative: instead of $M(R)$, may write down 2 equations and eliminate the normal reaction at $R$, $S_R$, to obtain an equation in $M$ only: $(\uparrow)S_R=40g+30g+2.5g+Mg$; $M(P)$: $42.5g\times 5+30g\times 2.5=3S_R$; $M(Q)$: $Mg\times 5+30g\times 2.5=2S_R$; $M(G)$: $Mg\times 2.5+0.5S_R=42.5g\times 2.5$. Equations must have correct no. of terms and be dimensionally correct but M0 if reaction at $P$ is non-zero. $M=\frac{70}{3}$, 23 or better A1: $\frac{70}{3}$ oe or 23 or better. Accept 24.

parts.text:
A small metal box of mass $6\,\mathrm{kg}$ is attached at $B$ to two ropes $BP$ and $BQ$. The fixed points $P$ and $Q$ are on a horizontal ceiling and $PQ=3.5\,\mathrm{m}$. The box hangs in equilibrium at a vertical distance of $2\,\mathrm{m}$ below the line $PQ$, with the ropes in a vertical plane and with angle $BQP=45^\circ$, as shown in Figure 3. The box is modelled as a particle and the ropes are modelled as light inextensible strings. Find

(i) the tension in $BP$,

(ii) the tension in $BQ$.
(10)
parts.mark_scheme: $PM=3.5-2\tan 45^\circ=1.5$ OR $PB=\sqrt{3.5^2+(\frac{2}{\sin 45^\circ})^2-2\times 3.5\times(\frac{2}{\sin 45^\circ})\cos 45^\circ}=2.5$ M1: finding the length of $PM$ or $PB$. $\tan\alpha=\frac{1.5}{2}$; $\cos\alpha=\frac{4}{5}$; $\sin\alpha=\frac{3}{5}$ OR $\alpha=37^\circ$ or $(90^\circ-\alpha)=53^\circ$ (at least 2SF) A1: correct trig ratio for $\alpha$ or $(90^\circ-\alpha)$ or a correct value for $\alpha$ or $(90^\circ-\alpha)$. Do not penalise accuracy here if their final answers for the tensions are correct. N.B. If they assume the tensions are the same, no further marks available. If they think $\alpha=30$ or $60$ or..., they could get all 5 resolving marks as a value of $\alpha$ is not required but if $\alpha=45$, only M marks available. However, if $\alpha$ and $45$ are interchanged in the resolving equations - no marks available for resolving. $T_P\cos\alpha+T_Q\cos 45^\circ=6g$ M1 A2 -1 ee: resolving vertically with usual rules, correct equation ($\alpha$ does not need to be substituted) -1 each error. $T_P\sin\alpha=T_Q\cos 45^\circ$ M1 A1: resolving horizontally with usual rules, correct equation ($\alpha$ does not need to be substituted but if it is, follow through on their value). $T_P=\frac{30g}{7}=42$ N; $T_Q=36$ or $35.6$ N DM1 A1; A1: dependent on all THREE previous M marks, for solving for either tension; $T_P$ allow 42.0, units not needed; $T_Q$, units not needed. Alternative, using Triangle of Forces/Lami's Theorem, for middle 5 marks: $\frac{T_P}{\sin 45^\circ}=\frac{6g}{\sin(45^\circ+\alpha)}$ OR $\frac{T_Q}{\sin(180^\circ-\alpha)}=\frac{6g}{\sin(45^\circ+\alpha)}$ M1 A2 -1 ee; $\frac{T_Q}{\sin(180^\circ-\alpha)}=\frac{6g}{\sin(45^\circ+\alpha)}$ OR $\frac{T_P}{\sin 45^\circ}=\frac{6g}{\sin(45^\circ+\alpha)}$ OR $\frac{T_P}{\sin 45^\circ}=\frac{T_Q}{\sin(180^\circ-\alpha)}$ M1 A1. N.B. Treat omission of $g$ as one error.

The train starts from rest at $A$ and moves with constant acceleration for $60\,\mathrm{s}$ until it reaches a speed of $V\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The train then travels at this constant speed $V\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ before it moves with constant deceleration for $30\,\mathrm{s}$, coming to rest at $B$.
